steps.name: Implement planMerge — the merge is a plan, not a write (GREEN)
criteria: Harvester-owned columns are always overwritten with the freshly derived value (DR-0004).
Human-owned columns never appear in an update's cells at all — not written, not referenced.
Columns the harvester does not recognise are never referenced by the plan, neither in appendColumns nor in any update.
A tracker key absent from the harvest appears nowhere in the plan — never updated, never removed (DR-0004 rule 1).
A blank Dedup Key is never a merge target, and its row's content appears nowhere in the plan (DR-0004 rule 2).
Harvester-owned columns missing from the sheet header are listed in appendColumns; no existing column moves, and sheetState is not mutated (DR-0004 rule 3).
A harvested key absent from the tracker is appended as a full row with every human-owned column blank.
Harvester-owned cells whose value changed between runs are reported in plan.changes as {key, column, from, to} (DR-0004 rule 4).
planMerge is pure: repeated calls on the same inputs deep-equal, and neither argument is mutated.
The __SCAFFOLD__ marker is removed from src/core/merge.mjs.
The suite gains 9 passing tests and loses none: 110 passed / 7 failed / 1 skipped.
steps.scenario_name: planMerge (DR-0004, DR-0005) — the merge is a plan, not a write
steps.implementation_notes: The 9 acceptance tests already exist, authored by DISTILL, and are the specification — this is a GREEN-the-ATs step, not a test-authoring step. Read DR-0004 (every column has exactly one owner) and DR-0005 (the target sheet is a plan-executing port) first; between them they carry the merge policy, the four rules, and the reason the plan is a value rather than a write. WritePlan shape per the existing JSDoc at merge.mjs:48 — {tab, appendColumns, updates: [{key, cells}], appends: [row], changes: [{key, column, from, to}]}. Two tests assert on JSON.stringify(plan) NOT containing a string, so an absent or blank-key row must not leak into any field including changes. Determinism is asserted directly (repeated calls deep-equal), so no timestamps, no Date.now, no iteration over unordered structures without sorting. DESIGN NOTE, deliberately NOT to be resolved here: HARVESTER_COLUMNS includes First Seen, Last Seen and Times Seen, which change on every run, so plan.changes will report them constantly and may drown the parser-improvement signal DR-0004 rule 4 exists to surface. The tests do not pin this either way. Implement exactly to the tests, add NO exclusion list, and report the concern — a filter would be new behaviour and needs its own acceptance test.
